title: Microkeratome-assisted ultrathin Descemet's stripping automated endothelial keratoplasty: A randomized trial comparing single-pass versus double-pass technique

groups.description: Group 1: graft prepared with a single slow microkeratome pass (400-um head); microkeratome-assisted ultrathin DSAEK (Descemet membrane scored and stripped, 9-mm mark, Busin glide insertion through a 3.2-mm tunnel, full air fill) for pseudophakic bullous keratopathy with a stable posterior chamber IOL; randomized pilot trial, single surgeon; eyes already pseudophakic, no same-session cataract surgery

Group 2: graft prepared with a double-pass technique (debulking and refinement cuts by the nomograms of Tables 1-2); two donor corneas with preparation complications (irregular cut, perforation) were not transplanted and were excluded by the authors; microkeratome-assisted ultrathin DSAEK (Descemet membrane scored and stripped, 9-mm mark, Busin glide insertion through a 3.2-mm tunnel, full air fill) for pseudophakic bullous keratopathy with a stable posterior chamber IOL; randomized pilot trial, single surgeon; eyes already pseudophakic, no same-session cataract surgery

notes: 20 eyes of 20 patients were randomized with a random-number table that allowed duplicate numbers; the article reports no group sizes, so n is null.
Both arms are standard graft-preparation techniques compared without an investigational agent, so both are role control; neither is declared the experimental arm.

The two group-2 donor corneas that failed during preparation were never transplanted (an intraoperative tissue event, not a postoperative outcome); the article does not say whether those eyes received another graft.
No graft detachment, infection, rejection or failure was observed postoperatively (Results).

Table 4 (uncorrected acuity), Table 6 (spherical equivalent), Table 7 (contrast sensitivity), Table 8 (central corneal thickness), Tables 9-10 (graft thickness) and Table 11 (endothelial cell density) are not used.
